issues.description: The problem statement (UML) specifies a Stock method named emptyStock(): void, and the reference solution implements emptyStock(). However, the template repository's Stock class provides a method named clearInventory() instead of emptyStock(). This name mismatch is structural (part of the public API students must use) and can confuse students about which method to call or cause compiler errors when students follow the UML/problem description or the solution examples that expect emptyStock().
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template Stock API match the problem statement and reference solution by renaming clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add an emptyStock() method that delegates to clearInventory(). This ensures students can follow the UML/specification and the solution examples without compilation issues.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and the solution implementation declare a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template repository provides a method named clearInventory() instead. This is a direct identifier naming mismatch for the same conceptual operation (clearing the stock). Students reading the problem will look for emptyStock() or be expected to implement behavior under that name, but the template uses clearInventory(), creating confusion and a likely mismatch with automated tests or graders that expect emptyStock().
issues.suggested_fix: Align the template with the problem statement and solution by renaming the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add a delegating emptyStock() method that calls clearInventory(). This makes the API consistent across problem, template, and solution and removes unnecessary mapping overhead for students.
